reading.body:
NTT Chicago CH1 in Itasca, Illinois, publishes 36 MW of IT capacity, operated by NTT.

At 10 kW per rack, a common enterprise colocation density, that load supports roughly 3600 racks. At 40 kW per rack, a density closer to AI training workloads, it supports roughly 900 racks. The operator has not published a per-rack power envelope, so neither figure is the operator's own claim, only what the published megawattage implies under each assumption.

No compliance certifications are published for NTT Chicago CH1. That does not mean none exist, only that this site's dataset, built from the operator's own facility page, does not list any, which limits what regulated workloads a reader could confirm the facility is qualified to host.

Illinois has 13 facilities mapped in this site's dataset, of which 6 publish a megawatt figure, totaling 236 MW. NTT Chicago CH1 contributes 36 MW of that total. That is a meaningful facility by colocation standards, though still below the scale where frontier AI training clusters typically operate.
